title: Analogies 2: name the relationship
description: Twenty analogies built around the five ways analogy questions are usually lost: choosing a pair from the same topic instead of the same relationship, reversing the order of a strong and a mild word, missing a relationship of lacking something, matching a part to a whole at the wrong size, and confusing what a thing is for with what it goes with. Before you look at the choices, say the relationship as a sentence, such as "an anchor holds a ship still." Then try each choice in that sentence. Thirty seconds each.

questions.explanation: An anchor holds a ship still once it has stopped, and a kickstand holds a bicycle still once it has stopped. Every other pair is about boats or the sea, which is the trap: the same topic, a different relationship. Sail is to wind is the closest of them, and it describes what moves a boat, the opposite of what an anchor does.

A stethoscope is an instrument for sensing something you could not otherwise hear, a heartbeat. A telescope is an instrument for sensing something you could not otherwise see, a planet. The other pairs all come from a doctor's office, and none of them is an instrument paired with what it detects. Bandage is to wound is the strongest trap, but a bandage covers a wound rather than detecting it.

A librarian looks after and organises a collection of books. A curator looks after and organises a collection of paintings in a museum. Reader is to novel and student is to library stay in the world of books, which is why they tempt, but a reader uses books rather than caring for a collection. Author is to story is maker to product, a different relationship.

A pharmacy is a shop that sells medicine, and a newsstand is a shop that sells magazines, so the relationship is shop to what it sells. Every other choice borrows a word from medicine, so it looks related, but doctor is to illness is a person to what they treat, and pill is to bottle is contents to container.

A drizzle is light rain and a downpour is heavy rain, so the pair runs from mild to strong. A breeze is a light wind and a gale is a strong one, mild to strong in the same order. Blizzard is to flurry and flood is to puddle are also pairs of strong and weak, but in the reverse order, strong first. Checking the direction is the whole question.

Furious is a much stronger form of annoyed, and the strong word comes first. Terrified is a much stronger form of uneasy, also strong first. Glad is to ecstatic is the right kind of pair in the wrong order, mild first, which is the mistake this question is built to catch. Calm is to angry is a pair of opposites, not two strengths of one feeling.

To nibble is to eat in tiny bites and to devour is to eat greedily, so the pair runs from a little to a lot of the same action. To sip is to drink a little and to gulp is to drink a lot quickly, in the same order. Feast is to snack is reversed, big first. Chew is to swallow is a sequence, one step after another, rather than two strengths of the same thing.

Ancient means extremely old, so the pair is an extreme word followed by the ordinary word for the same quality. Minuscule means extremely small, followed by small. Large is to enormous has the ordinary word first and the extreme one second, the reverse. New is to old is a pair of opposites, and antique is to valuable is an association, since old things are sometimes worth a lot.

Barren land has no vegetation, so the relationship is a word meaning without something, followed by the thing it is without. Anonymous means without a name. Fertile is to crops, garden is to flowers and forest is to trees all pair something with what it has, which is the opposite relationship. Desert is to sand also pairs a place with what it contains.

A timid person lacks boldness, and a clumsy person lacks grace. Brave is to courage, loud is to noise and nervous is to fear all pair a quality with something it has rather than something it lacks: the words clearly belong together, but the relationship is turned around. Shy is to quiet is close to a pair of synonyms.

Inaudible means impossible to hear, and illegible means impossible to read. Visible and edible are the positive forms, able to be seen and able to be eaten, so they reverse the relationship. Fragile means easily broken, which is still something that can happen, not something that cannot. Watch for in or il at the front of the stem word: it often means not.

A blackout is a complete absence of electricity, and a vacuum is a complete absence of air. Flood is to water is the trap: it is the opposite, too much of something rather than none of it. Battery is to power and lamp is to light pair a source with what it gives, which is close in topic to electricity and nothing like an absence.

A verse is one of the main sections a song is divided into, and a stanza is one of the main sections a poem is divided into. Note is to melody and letter is to alphabet are also part to whole, which makes them tempting, but a note or a letter is a far smaller piece. The right answer matches the size of the part as well as the fact of being a part. Album is to track puts the whole first.

An archipelago is a named group of islands, so an island is one member of the group. A star is one member of a constellation. Ocean is to wave puts the larger thing first, the reverse. Valley is to mountain and lighthouse is to shore are things found next to each other, not a member and its group.

A wall is built from many bricks fitted together, and a mosaic is built from many tiles fitted together, so the relationship is a single repeated unit to the thing it builds. Clay is to pottery is material to product, which sounds similar but is different: pottery is made of clay, not assembled from separate pieces of it. Mason is to trowel is worker to tool.

A book is divided into chapters and a video game is divided into levels: each is one of the large sections the whole is built from, taken in order. Word is to sentence is part to whole too, but a word is a tiny piece, the way a line is a tiny piece of a poem. Season is to episode is reversed, since a season contains episodes. Matching the size of the part is what separates the right answer from the near miss.

The purpose of a sieve is to strain, and the purpose of a pump is to inflate, so the relationship is a tool to the job it is built for. Kitchen is to cook is the trap: cooking happens in a kitchen, but a kitchen is a place, not a tool. Bowl is to soup is a container to what it holds, and chef is to stir is a person to one of the things they do.

A vaccine exists to protect, and a lighthouse exists to warn ships away from danger, so the relationship is a thing to its purpose. Needle is to sharp pairs a thing with a quality it has, not a purpose. Illness is to cure pairs a problem with its solution, which sounds medical but is a different relationship.

A sketch is the rough plan an artist makes before the finished painting, and an outline is the plan a writer makes before the finished essay. Frame is to picture stays with art, which tempts, but a frame surrounds a finished picture rather than coming before it. Statue is to sculpture is close to a pair of synonyms.

A leash is held by a person to guide and control a dog, and a rein is held by a rider to guide and control a horse. Bone is to puppy and bark is to dog stay with dogs, which is the topic trap. Saddle is to rider is close, since a saddle is riding equipment, but a saddle is for sitting on, not for steering the animal.
